caption:
Gen Z is now 26% of India's workforce — nearly double its 2023 share. That cohort does not hand you authority because of your title or your years served.

So you are squeezed from both sides. Above you, your ideas land only when someone else repeats them. Below you, a quarter of your people are measuring whether you are worth following — and 93% of Indian Gen Zs are already asking AI for career advice instead of asking you.

Positional authority is what the org chart grants. Earned authority is what the room concedes. One is printed. The other is demonstrated — in bearing, in tone, in the silence you hold before you answer.

Colonel Suhag spent 35 years in command, where no one follows rank alone under pressure. The Lumina Method translates that into what you do in Monday's meeting.

Rank gets you the room. Command keeps it.

topic.title: Gen Z is 26% of the workforce — authority must be earned
topic.angle: Lumina's buyers manage this cohort and now face a two-directional authority problem — overlooked upward while leading a quarter of the workforce that doesn't grant authority on title or tenure — which is precisely Colonel Suhag's earned-versus-positional authority material.
topic.why_now: A 15 October 2026 synthesis of Great Place To Work, Naukri and Deloitte data put Gen Z's share at 26% — nearly double 2023 — and the threshold crossing is being actively discussed in Indian HR media this month, alongside the finding that 93% of Indian Gen Zs now use AI for career advice.

rationale: A stark text-only visual matches the caption's blunt earned-versus-positional contrast and keeps the focus on the line that carries the argument.
